components.FileUpload:
<>

Drop a few images (or click to browse) — max 4 files, 2 MB each. The upload transport below is entirely simulated (staged progress ticks, ~20% chance of a failure to show the Retry action) since toolcrib takes no opinion on the backend protocol: onUpload is just a consumer-supplied (file, onProgress) => Promise<void>.

new Promise((resolve, reject) => { let pct = 0; const tick = () => { pct += 20; onProgress(Math.min(pct, 100)); if (pct < 100) { setTimeout(tick, 250); } else if (Math.random() < 0.2) { reject(new Error('Simulated network error')); } else { addToast({ type: 'success', message: `${file.name} uploaded`, priority: 'low' }); resolve(); } }; setTimeout(tick, 250); }) } />

The Form component provides automatic Zod 4 schema validation, field registration, error layout, and touched field tracking without prop-drilling.

systems.resilience:
Catch Render Crashes (`<AIErrorBoundary>`)

Wraps a subtree so a render error there shows a fallback instead of crashing the whole page — the same boundary Modal/Drawer/AlertDialog already wrap their own content in internally. It also emits error:boundary on the bus (see this card's top-right toast — that subscription is separate from the log panel below, forwarding just this one event as a real app would).
